clue.text: Erode article seen in river path

indicators.note: the article is seen sitting inside the run of the river and the path, between the two words

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham
a way is a path or route
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something is eroding a riverside path, with an article about it appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in County Durham, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away is to erode gradually by friction or weathering, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Merited getting time for violence initially? Ran off

indicators.note: the word for merited gets something new in place of a letter, signalling a swap
time for violence says the letter for time stands where the violence letter was

parts.note: merited means deserved

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of violence is used

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a punishment was earned, getting time for violent behaviour, then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'for' together swap the V of DESERVED for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted is the past tense of desert, to abandon or run away, matching ran off.

clue.text: Nobleman appointed to receive King

indicators.note: the word for appointed takes in the king letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: due means appointed or scheduled, as in the due time
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nobleman has been appointed to welcome the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, so a nobleman by title.

clue.text: Unit expert heading off, maintaining skill leading soldiers

indicators.note: maintaining means holding within, so the trimmed expert word contains the rest
the expert word loses its first letter, its heading

parts.note: an adept is an expert

indicators.note: skill comes leading, that is in front of, the soldiers

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A military unit where a top expert departs but skill is kept up at the head of the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks military alongside 'soldiers', but it means a section of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a section or division of an organisation, so a unit of it.

clue.text: French city name offered amongst friends in Paris

indicators.note: the name letter goes amongst the letters of the French friends

parts.note: amies is French for female friends

explanation.surface: Someone names a French city when chatting with friends in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France, capital of Picardy, famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: Rapacity keeps Australian state area reduced by 50%: grassy area?

indicators.note: the rapacity word keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: rapacity means greed
NSW is New South Wales, an Australian state

indicators.note: only the first half of the word area is used

explanation.surface: Greedy developers grab an Australian state's land, cut in half: a grassy area?
explanation.walkthrough: Halving a four-letter word keeps its first two letters. Greensward is a literary word, so the question mark signals a fanciful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensward is literary for turf or a stretch of grass-covered ground.

clue.text: Remove restriction from European pistol back in time

indicators.note: the European and pistol letters are placed in the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: back means the pistol's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol

explanation.surface: Taking the controls off a European gun brought back in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Luger is a German pistol, a name crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: To deregulate is to free an activity from rules or controls.

clue.text: Given burden, not small, not well organised

indicators.note: not means the small letter is left out of the burden word

parts.note: saddled means given a burden
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Weighed down with responsibility but not small, and not well organised.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or confused, describing thinking without order.

clue.text: Make no progress when the results come out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stay in place without advancing
second meaning, playful: the ... of ..., when exam results are produced

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a punning one: marking time is the period when papers are marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching soldiers mark time by stepping on the spot, hence idle waiting; read literally, it is the period for marking.

clue.text: About to pierce gem setting, cutting end — an easy matter

indicators.note: the about word pierces, going into the trimmed gem setting
the last letter of the gem setting word is cut off

parts.note: a bezel is the rim that holds a gemstone in place
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A jeweller describing working on a stone setting, saying it's easy.
explanation.walkthrough: A bezel is the metal rim that grips a stone in a ring or watch face.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is informal for something done with no effort at all.

clue.text: Servant returned to English terrace from 12 to 6?

indicators.note: returned means the servant word is read backwards

parts.note: a maid is a servant
Ter. is the abbreviation for terrace in street addresses

explanation.surface: A maid heading back to an English row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Ter. is a British address abbreviation, like St or Rd. On a clock face, a line from 12 to 6 passes straight through the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is a straight line across a circle through its centre, as between 12 and 6 on a clock.

clue.text: Relaxation of strained relations not completely covering slip — justification for armaments?

indicators.note: the trimmed relaxation word covers, going round, the slip word
the last letter is missing, so the word is incomplete

parts.note: detente is the easing of hostility between nations
to err is to slip up or make a mistake

explanation.surface: Cold War politics: an easing of tension masking a blunder, used to justify weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase is a dictionary-style definition of detente, used as a single piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuclear deterrent argument holds that weapons prevent attack, so it justifies having them.

clue.text: Cut joke about revolutionary sex after protest supported by the people

indicators.note: the cut joke part comes after the protest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the cut joke word goes about, surrounding, the reversed sex word
the joke word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a crack is a joke or wisecrack

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: it is informal for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A cutting joke about revolutionary sex after a protest, backed by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as slang for sex is a crossword staple; 'revolutionary' here means turned round, not political.
explanation.definitionFit: Democratic means based on the will of the people, so having popular backing.

clue.text: Sought vaguely to interrupt bird violence

indicators.note: the rearranged letters break into the bird word

parts.note: a ruff is a wading bird, the male of which has a showy collar

indicators.note: vaguely signals the letters of sought are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely looking interrupts a bird, causing violence.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruff is a wading bird, named for the frilled collar of the breeding male.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough stuff is informal for violent or aggressive behaviour.

clue.text: Son remains in band

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A son's ashes are kept in a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Hollywood film produced in America in two versions

indicators.note: the produced word sits in between the two forms of America

parts.note: A and US are two standard ways of writing America, placed one either side
made means produced

explanation.surface: A Hollywood film made in America, released in two cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A and US are both abbreviations for America; MADE goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus is the 1984 Oscar-winning film by Milos Forman about Mozart.

clue.text: Impassive cathedral dignitary detaining Dutch father

indicators.note: the dignitary holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a dean is the head of a cathedral chapter
pa is informal for father

explanation.surface: A stony-faced church official holding a Dutch priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan means showing no emotion, delivered with a blank face.

clue.text: Particular kind of suit required for ice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
second meaning: ice is slang for ..., the jewels

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clothing for cold weather; suit is the card sense and ice the slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is a card suit, and ice is underworld slang for diamond jewellery.

clue.text: Moustache regulation upheld: plan to get trimmed

indicators.note: in a down clue, upheld means the word is held up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a law is a regulation

indicators.note: the plan word is trimmed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a ruse is a crafty plan

explanation.surface: A rule on facial hair is upheld, and a scheme to keep it trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: LAW reversed is WAL; RUSE trimmed is RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick drooping one, like the animal's whiskers.

clue.text: Rogue hiding piano in trick

indicators.note: the piano letter is hidden away, so it disappears from the rogue word

parts.note: a scamp is a rogue or rascal
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A rascal concealing a piano as part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme or swindle, a kind of trick.

clue.text: Attractive item in painting finally captured by French painter

indicators.note: the final letter is captured inside the painter's name

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French painter

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of painting

explanation.surface: An appealing object in a picture, the last one taken by a French artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet attracts iron, so it is literally an attractive item.

clue.text: First of Tories brought in to try and secure important region

indicators.note: the Tory letter is brought into the middle of the other two words

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
to land a deal is to secure it

indicators.note: only the first letter of Tories is used

explanation.surface: A Conservative is brought in to try to win over a key area.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party. HEAR as in a judge hearing, that is trying, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartland is a central area of key importance, such as a party's core support.

clue.text: Child beginning to dismiss response to joke, having missed opening

indicators.note: beginning to dismiss means the first letter of dismiss
the joke response loses its opening letter

parts.note: laughter is the response to a joke

explanation.surface: A child starts to brush off laughter at a joke, having missed the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female offspring, so someone's child.

clue.text: Composer heads for dreary violinist over scraping? Not half

indicators.note: the heads are the first letters of the three words
only half of the scraping word is kept, its first half

parts.note: raking means scraping, as with a rake

explanation.surface: A dull violinist going on scraping away at a composer's music; not half!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much'. RAKING halved is RAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak was the Czech composer of the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Diehard missing regular items is no longer active

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, leaving the alternate letters

explanation.surface: Even a diehard who skips events eventually stops taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the second, fourth and sixth letters of DIEHARD leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead can mean inactive or defunct, as in a dead account or a dead issue.

clue.text: See 1
See 9
Singular conclusions in Cardiff glass works — benefit for the Treasury?

indicators.note: works signals the letters being worked into a new order
the doubled endings of both words are made single, one letter each dropped

explanation.surface: A singular end product from glass works in Cardiff, a boon for the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: CARDIFF and GLASS each end in a double letter; making them single gives CARDIF and GLAS, which are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal drag is when inflation pushes earners into higher tax bands, raising tax revenue without a rate rise.
